mechanism_narrative: Transit-station mobility recovered 11 points in three weeks (-27.7 at t-3w to -16.7 at t-0w). Because transit use is a precondition for discretionary trips, this run-rate continues and RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days averages above the -34.4 mean of the last 28 days.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose from -37.9 at t-3w to -28.3 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is at or below the -34.4 mean of the last 28 days even though TRANSIT continues to rise.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM crossed from -16.1 to +0.3 percent of baseline within three weeks, showing that essential-trip normalization is complete. Once grocery and pharmacy trips are at baseline, the marginal household rupee shifts to non-essential channels, lifting RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above 0 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM crossed zero at t-0w with +0.3
failure_condition: In the two weeks after GROCERY_PHARM holds at or above 0, RETAIL_REC never exceeds its t-0w level of -28.3.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL excess fell from +7.9 to +5.1 while TRANSIT rose simultaneously, which marks substitution of stay-at-home time for out-of-home trips. The joint condition (RESIDENTIAL falling and TRANSIT rising) is the trigger; it drives a higher 28-day RETAIL_REC mean than the trailing one.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below +6.0 and TRANSIT rises in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell 7.9 to 5.1 while TRANSIT rose -27.7 to -16.7
failure_condition: In weeks where RESIDENTIAL falls below +6.0 and TRANSIT rises together, forward 28-day RETAIL_REC is not higher than the trailing 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS is the fastest-recovering out-of-home category (-39.0 to -28.7 over three weeks), consistent with late-winter weather improvement. Outdoor leisure trips spill into adjacent retail-and-recreation venues, so RETAIL_REC rises within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS improves by more than 5 points over two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS gained 10.3 points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: PARKS keeps improving but RETAIL_REC two weeks later does not exceed its t-0w value of -28.3.

mechanism_narrative: The unwinding of the residential excess (-7.9 to +5.1) shows households reverting to pre-pandemic routines. As time spent at home converges toward baseline, weekday retail footfall recovers, so RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks is higher than over the last four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL prints below +6.0 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined every week from 7.9 at t-3w to 5.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: While RESIDENTIAL stays below +6.0, the forward 28-day RETAIL_REC mean is not higher than the last 28-day mean of -34.4.

mechanism_narrative: Renewed containment in Delhi registers first in transit stations. If TRANSIT drops more than 8 points week-on-week, discretionary retail footfall contracts the following week, dragging the forward 28-day RETAIL_REC mean below the current trailing level.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 8 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES flat at -23.4 then -23.6 in the last two weeks
failure_condition: TRANSIT falls more than 8 points in a week and RETAIL_REC in the following week is still at or above the trailing four-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: The recovery is broad-based rather than essential-only: GROCERY_PHARM, PARKS and TRANSIT all improved in the final week simultaneously, a pattern that essential shopping alone cannot produce. This joint breadth forces a fast RETAIL_REC rebound within one week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM, PARKS and TRANSIT all improve week-on-week in the same print
evidence_refs: fact:t-0w shows simultaneous gains in GROCERY_PHARM, PARKS and TRANSIT
failure_condition: After a week in which all three series rise together, RETAIL_REC does not improve on its t-0w value of -28.3.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES stalled (-23.4 then -23.6) while every other series advanced, and RESIDENTIAL remains above baseline. A stalled office recovery plus persistent work-from-home caps weekday retail demand, so the next 28-day RETAIL_REC mean fails to beat the last.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES stays below -20 and RESIDENTIAL stays above +5 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES flat at -23.4 then -23.6 across t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: While WORKPLACES stays below -20 and RESIDENTIAL above +5, the forward 28-day RETAIL_REC mean exceeds the last 28-day mean of -34.4.
